answer.generated: Transparency in distributed systems engineering refers to the extent to which users perceive the system as a single, unified entity rather than a collection of separate components. A distributed system appears transparent when its distributed nature is hidden from the user, meaning interactions seem local and consistent regardless of physical location. This transparency is crucial for usability and ease of use, as it allows users to interact without being aware of underlying network or system architecture.
